tools.name: updateScript
tools.description:
[write] PUT /scripts/:scriptId — Updates scenario metadata including name, code (main/init/teardown), and declared parameters
(`paramsConfig`).

**IMPORTANT — always keep `paramsConfig` in sync with the code**: Whenever you add, rename,
or remove a parameter reference in the script code (e.g. `process.env.URL`,
`${__P(threads)}`, `System.getProperty("users")`, `os.environ.get('CLIENTS')`), you MUST
also update `paramsConfig` in the same call to declare (or remove) the corresponding
parameter. Failing to do so means the parameter will not appear in test configurations and
users will have no prompt to supply a value.

**Workflow when parameterizing code:**
1. Update the script code to read the parameter (e.g. `const url = process.env.URL || 'https://example.com'`).
2. In the same `PUT /scripts/{scriptId}` call, include the updated `paramsConfig` array with
   the new parameter entry (`name`, `required`, `defaultValue`).

**After updating a scenario:** Run a smoke test using the `run_smoke_test` tool with this script ID. Verify the result: check that `passed` is `true`, `status` is `"finished"`, and review `diagnostics`, `logs`, `suiteResults`, `suiteTestResults`, result events, and assertions for errors or failed assertions. Treat `passed=false`, `diagnostics.reasons`, error/fatal log lines, failed suite tests/assertions, or a finished smoke test with empty suite results and no result events as a failed smoke test. Fix scenario script/configuration issues and rerun smoke tests until the scenario passes or a real external blocker prevents progress. Only after the smoke test looks good should you start a full test execution or report that the scenario is ready.

**Proactive app inspection for browser/OpenFin scenario updates:** If the user asks you to inspect, explore,
look at, browse, or understand a browser app or OpenFin app while updating this scenario, launch and inspect the
app with the browser tools before finalizing the update. Use `browser_launch`/`browser_navigate` for web apps;
use `browser_launch(openfinConfigUrl=...)` plus `browser_pages`, `browser_switch_page`, screenshots, content/title
inspection, and evaluation for OpenFin apps.
 Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

main.description: Main script contents (base64 encoded or plain text depending on scenario type)

init.description: Init script contents (runs once before the test)

teardown.description: Teardown script contents (runs once after the test)

paramsConfig.description:
Full replacement list of declared parameters for this scenario. Pass the complete
desired list — any parameter omitted from this array will be removed.

**Always include this when parameterizing code.** For example, if you update a
Playwright script to read `process.env.URL`, add `{name: "url", required: false,
defaultValue: "https://example.com"}` here. If you update a JMeter plan to use
`${__P(threads)}`, add `{name: "threads", required: false, defaultValue: "50"}`.

name.description:
Parameter name. Accessible at runtime as an environment variable with the name
uppercased (e.g. `baseUrl` → `BASE_URL`). For JMeter, also accessible as a JMeter
property via `${__P(name)}`. For Gatling, via `System.getProperty("name")`.

required.description: Whether this parameter must be provided by the configuration. Defaults to false.

defaultValue.description: Default value used when the configuration does not supply one.

scriptType.description: Scenario type (only needed when converting type)

providers.description:
**IMPORTANT**: Array of test runner source entries. Each object MUST contain `providerId`,
`params`, and `numRegions`. The `params` field is INSIDE each entry, not a top-level field.

**Correct structure:**
```json
"providers": [{"providerId": 2, "params": {"regions": "1", "weight": "100"}, "numRegions": 1}]
```

See CreateConfiguration schema for detailed documentation of params by test runner source type.

params.description:
**CRITICAL**: This `params` object must be nested INSIDE each test runner source entry, not at the configuration level.
See CreateConfiguration schema for detailed documentation of required and optional params by source type.

numRegions.description:
Number of regions this test runner source entry covers:
- For Shared Grid sources: Set to the count of regions in the comma-separated `regions` param
- For OnDemand sources: Always 1 (create separate entries for each region)

testType.description: Type of test (Load for multiple users, Functional for single user, Monitor for recurring functional tests)

profileType.description: Load profile type (not supported for JMeter, Gatling, Locust)

durationSecs.description: Duration of the test in seconds (mutually exclusive with iterations)

iterations.description: Number of times to execute the scenario per concurrent client (mutually exclusive with durationSecs, only for Flat profiles)

iterationSleepSecs.description: Sleep time in seconds between iterations

rampupSecs.description: Time to ramp up to desired concurrent clients (only for Flat profiles)

concurrentClients.description: Number of concurrent users per region (for Step profiles, this is the ending number)

startConcurrentClients.description: Starting number of concurrent clients (only for Step profiles)

step.description: Concurrent clients to add per step (only for Step profiles)

loadType.description:
**FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING (multi-user) SCENARIO TYPES ONLY**: Controls how virtual user
load is managed. Use `Basic` (the default) unless the user explicitly requests otherwise.
With `Advanced`, Testable does not inject standard load params automatically, but you can
still pass scenario params via `scriptParams` that the scenario explicitly reads (e.g.
`${__P(threads)}` in JMeter, `System.getProperty("users")` in Gatling, env vars in Locust).
See CreateConfiguration for full documentation.

scriptParams.description:
JSON string of scenario parameter key/value pairs to pass to the scenario at runtime.
See CreateConfiguration for full documentation including Locust/JMeter/Gatling guidance.

imageDiffMode.description: Image comparison mode for scenarios that support screenshot capture

deleteSchedule.description: Set to true to delete associated schedule

useDefaultNotifications.description:
When `true`, the test configuration uses the organization's default notification
channels. When `false`, the configuration uses the `notifications` array below.
Omitted or unchanged when not updating notification settings.

notifications.description:
Per-test notification channels. Used only when `useDefaultNotifications` is `false`.
Replaces any existing test-level notifications. Each entry configures when to notify
(on success/failure) and the destination (email, Slack, Teams, HTTP, etc.).

notificationMedium.description:
Channel type. `Email`, `Text`, `Voice`, `WhatsApp` for messaging; `HTTP` for webhooks;
`Slack`, `Teams`, `SNS` when those integrations are enabled for the org.

successNotificationStyle.description: When to send a notification on test success. `First` = first success only; `Always` = every success; `None` = never.

failureNotificationStyle.description: When to send a notification on test failure. `First` = first failure only; `Always` = every failure (subject to repeat); `None` = never.

failureNotificationConsecutiveTimes.description: Number of consecutive failures before sending (when failure style is First).

notificationTarget.description:
For Email medium only: `OrgEmail` uses the org's default email; `CustomList` uses
`customNotificationList` (or org default if empty).

customNotificationList.description:
Destination for this channel. Email address for Email; Slack channel or webhook URL for
Slack; Teams channel ID or webhook for Teams; URL for HTTP; SNS topic etc. Optional for
OrgEmail; required for CustomList when the medium needs a target.

tools.name: createTestConf
tools.description:
[write] POST /test-cases/:testCaseId/confs — Creates a new test configuration (load profile + test runner sources) for a test case.

**Required before calling createTestConf:** ALWAYS get the full tool details for
`getTestRunnerSources` (call describe_tools with toolNames including getTestRunnerSources),
then call getTestRunnerSources to list available test runner sources and their IDs. Use
the returned source IDs as `providerId` in the providers array when calling createTestConf.
Do not call createTestConf without first calling getTestRunnerSources to discover providers.

**Test runner source selection (see Test Runners guide):** For tests with more than one
concurrent virtual user, use a public OnDemand source (*Per Test: Testable VPC/Virtual
Network* — AWS, Azure, or GCP) unless the user asks for something else. OnDemand =
instances spun up per test and terminated after; recommended for load testing. Use *Long
Running: Public Shared Grid* (Shared) only when the user explicitly requests it or
concurrency is very low (e.g. single virtual user smoke test). Use a private OnDemand
source (*Per Test: Your VPC/Virtual Network*) when the user has registered their cloud
account and chosen it as the source.

**Billing/runnability note for AI assistants:** The create response includes a `billing`
estimate. If that estimate has `possible=false` or a non-empty `explanation`, immediately
call `getTestConf` for the returned configuration ID and use the refreshed `billing` value
before telling the user whether the configuration is runnable. If the refreshed value still
reports `possible=false`, phrase it as "the latest configuration state reports billing
possible=false" and include the returned explanation; do not state categorically that the
test is not runnable unless a start/run tool has actually failed.
 Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

providers.description:
**IMPORTANT**: Array of test runner source entries. Each object MUST contain `providerId`
(test runner source ID), `params`, and `numRegions`. The `params` object is nested
INSIDE each entry, not at the top level of the configuration.

**Test runner source selection (Test Runners guide):** Prefer a public OnDemand source
(*Per Test: Testable VPC/Virtual Network* — AWS, Azure, or GCP) for tests with more than
one concurrent user. Use *Long Running: Public Shared Grid* (Shared) only when the user
explicitly requests it or concurrency is one (e.g. smoke test). Use a private OnDemand
source (*Per Test: Your VPC/Virtual Network*) when the user has registered their cloud
account and selected it.

**Example for Long Running Public Shared Grid:**
```json
"providers": [
  {
    "providerId": 2,
    "params": {
      "regions": "1",
      "weight": "100",
      "concurrentClients": "5"
    },
    "numRegions": 1
  }
]
```

**Example for AWS Per Test (Testable VPC or Your VPC):**
```json
"providers": [
  {
    "providerId": 5,
    "params": {
      "region": "us-east-1",
      "concurrentClients": 10,
      "weight": 100,
      "instanceType": "c5.xlarge",
      "ratio": 50,
      "nodes": 1
    },
    "numRegions": 1
  }
]
```

Use `GET /providers` to discover available test runner sources and their IDs.

params.description:
**CRITICAL**: This `params` object is REQUIRED and must be nested inside this
test runner source entry. Do NOT create a top-level `params` field in the configuration.

Parameters vary by test runner source type:

**For Shared sources (Long Running: Public Shared Grid, providerType='Shared'):**
- `regions` (required): Comma-separated list of region IDs (e.g., "1,5,10")
- `weight` (required): Comma-separated list of weights per region (e.g., "50,30,20"). Must sum to 100.
- `concurrentClients` (optional): Comma-separated concurrent users per region (e.g., "10,6,4")
- `startConcurrentClients` (optional, Step profile only): Comma-separated starting concurrent users
- `step` (optional, Step profile only): Comma-separated step increments
- `tags` (optional): Comma-separated agent tags to target specific agents
- `freeAgentsOnly` (optional): Comma-separated boolean strings ("true,false,true") to use only idle agents
- `maxAgents` (optional): Comma-separated max agents per region (e.g., "5,3,2")

**For AWS OnDemand public (Per Test: Testable VPC, source='Aws', public=true):**
- `region` (required): Native AWS region name (e.g., "us-east-1"). **Do NOT use the Shared source region identifier format** (e.g., NOT "aws-us-east-1") — that format is only for Public Shared Grid region IDs.
- `concurrentClients` (required): Number of concurrent users for this location
- `weight` (required): Weight for load distribution (0-100)
- `nodes` (optional): Number of EC2 instances (calculated from concurrentClients/ratio if not provided)
- `instanceType` (optional): EC2 instance type name (e.g., "c5.xlarge")
- `ratio` (optional): Concurrent users per instance
- `spot` (optional): "true" to use spot instances
- `spotMaxPrice` (optional): Max price for spot instances
- `image` (optional): AMI ID to use
- `instanceStrategy` (optional): Instance selection strategy ("Manual", "Automatic")
- `startConcurrentClients` (optional, Step profile only): Starting concurrent users
- `step` (optional, Step profile only): Step increment
- `enableElasticIps` (optional): "true" to use Elastic IPs
- `chooseAnyElasticIp` (optional): "true" to automatically select any available Elastic IP
- `forceAssociateElasticIps` (optional): "true" to force Elastic IP association
- `chosenElasticIps` (optional): Comma-separated list of specific Elastic IPs to use

**For AWS OnDemand private (Per Test: Your VPC, public=false):**
- All public AWS params above, plus:
- `vpc` (optional): VPC ID where instances will be launched
- `subnet` (optional): Subnet ID or "any" for automatic selection
- `keyPair` (optional): EC2 key pair name for SSH access
- `awsTags` (optional): JSON string of AWS tags array (e.g., '[{"key":"Environment","value":"Test"}]')

**For Azure OnDemand public (Per Test: Testable Virtual Network, source='Azure', public=true):**
- `region` (required): Azure region name (e.g., "eastus")
- `concurrentClients` (required): Number of concurrent users for this location
- `weight` (required): Weight for load distribution (0-100)
- `nodes` (optional): Number of VM instances
- `instanceType` (optional): Azure VM size (e.g., "Standard_D2s_v3")
- `ratio` (optional): Concurrent users per instance
- `lowPriority` (optional): "true" to use low priority VMs
- `image` (optional): Azure image ID to use
- `instanceStrategy` (optional): Instance selection strategy
- `startConcurrentClients` (optional, Step profile only): Starting concurrent users
- `step` (optional, Step profile only): Step increment
- `enablePublicIps` (optional): "true" to use public IPs
- `chooseAnyPublicIp` (optional): "true" to automatically select any available public IP
- `forceAssociatePublicIps` (optional): "true" to force public IP association
- `chosenPublicIps` (optional): Comma-separated list of specific public IPs to use

**For Azure OnDemand private (Per Test: Your Virtual Network, public=false):**
- All public Azure params above, plus:
- `resourceGroup` (optional): Azure resource group name or "[Automatic]"
- `network` (optional): Virtual network name or "[Automatic]"
- `subnet` (optional): Subnet name or "[Automatic]"
- `azureTags` (optional): JSON string of Azure tags array

**For GCP OnDemand public (Per Test: Testable Virtual Network, source='Gcp', public=true):**
- `region` (required): GCP region name (e.g., "us-east1")
- `concurrentClients` (required): Number of concurrent users for this location
- `weight` (required): Weight for load distribution (0-100)
- `nodes` (optional): Number of VM instances
- `instanceType` (optional): GCP machine type (e.g., "n1-standard-2")
- `ratio` (optional): Concurrent users per instance
- `image` (optional): GCP image ID to use
- `instanceStrategy` (optional): Instance selection strategy
- `startConcurrentClients` (optional, Step profile only): Starting concurrent users
- `step` (optional, Step profile only): Step increment

**For GCP OnDemand private (Per Test: Your Virtual Network, public=false):**
- All public GCP params above, plus:
- `network` (optional): VPC network name or "[Automatic]"
- `subnet` (optional): Subnet name or "[Automatic]"
- `zone` (optional): Specific zone within region, or empty for automatic selection
- `gcpTags` (optional): JSON string of GCP labels array

```json
  "params": {
    "region": "us-central1",
    "concurrentClients": 40,
    "weight": 100,
    "instanceType": "n1-standard-4",
    "ratio": 80,
    "nodes": 1
  },
  "numRegions": 1
}
```

**Example 10: GCP OnDemand Private (with network configuration)**
```json
{
  "providerId": 18,
  "params": {
    "region": "europe-west1",
    "concurrentClients": 60,
    "weight": 100,
    "instanceType": "n1-standard-8",
    "ratio": 100,
    "nodes": 1,
    "network": "default",
    "subnet": "default",
    "zone": "europe-west1-b",
    "gcpTags": "[{\"key\":\"environment\",\"value\":\"test\"}]"
  },
  "numRegions": 1
}
```

**Example 11: Step Profile (multiple regions, public shared grid)**
```json
{
  "providerId": 1,
  "params": {
    "regions": "1,5",
    "weight": "60,40",
    "concurrentClients": "30,20",
    "startConcurrentClients": "10,5",
    "step": "5,5"
  },
  "numRegions": 2
}
```

---

**Important notes:**
- **STRUCTURE**: This `params` object MUST be nested inside each entry in the providers array
- **WRONG**: `"providers": [{"providerId": 2, "numRegions": 1}], "params": {...}` (params at config level)
- **CORRECT**: `"providers": [{"providerId": 2, "params": {...}, "numRegions": 1}]` (params inside entry)
- For Shared sources, numRegions should match the count of comma-separated values in regions param
- For OnDemand sources, numRegions is always 1 (one region per entry)
- Step profile fields (startConcurrentClients, step) only apply when profileType='Step'
- Tags/labels JSON format: '[{"key":"name","value":"value"}]'
- Boolean values in params should be strings ("true" or "false"), not actual booleans

numRegions.description:
Number of regions this test runner source entry covers:
- For Shared Grid sources: Set to the count of regions in the comma-separated `regions` param
- For OnDemand sources: Always 1 (create separate entries for each region)

testType.description: Type of test (Load for multiple users, Functional for single user, Monitor for recurring functional tests)

profileType.description: Load profile type (not supported for JMeter, Gatling, Locust)

durationSecs.description:
Duration of the test in seconds (mutually exclusive with iterations).
**IMPORTANT FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING**: Do NOT use this field for these scenario types.
For JMeter/Gatling/Locust, duration is controlled by the engine itself via scenario parameters,
not at the Testable configuration level.

iterations.description:
Number of times to execute the scenario per concurrent client (mutually exclusive with durationSecs, only for Flat profiles).
**IMPORTANT FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING**: ALWAYS set this to 1 for these scenario types.
Each engine instance runs once, and the engine itself controls how long it runs and how many iterations/users it manages internally.

iterationSleepSecs.description:
Sleep time in seconds between iterations.
**IMPORTANT FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING**: Set this to 0 for these scenario types (no sleep between engine executions).

rampupSecs.description:
Time to ramp up to desired concurrent clients (only for Flat profiles).
**IMPORTANT FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING**: Set this to 0 for these scenario types.
Rampup is controlled by the engine itself via scenario parameters, not at the Testable configuration level.

concurrentClients.description:
Number of concurrent users per region (for Step profiles, this is the ending number).
**IMPORTANT FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING**: For these scenario types, this represents the number of ENGINE INSTANCES, NOT virtual users.
Each engine instance will then spawn its own virtual users as configured in the scenario or via scenario parameters.
For example, if you set concurrentClients=2 and pass threads=100 for JMeter, you'll get 2 JMeter engines each running 100 threads = 200 total virtual users.

startConcurrentClients.description: Starting number of concurrent clients (only for Step profiles)

step.description: Concurrent clients to add per step (only for Step profiles)

loadType.description:
**FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING (multi-user) SCENARIO TYPES ONLY**: Controls how virtual user load
is managed. Always use `Basic` unless the user explicitly requests otherwise.

- **Basic** (default): Testable manages load using standard scenario parameters passed via
  `scriptParams` (threads, users, clients, duration, rampup, etc.). All the guidance in the
  `scriptParams` field applies when `loadType` is `Basic`. This is the standard, recommended
  mode for most configurations.
- **Advanced**: The scenario manages load internally. Testable does not inject standard
  load parameters automatically. However, if the scenario is written to read parameters
  (e.g. a JMeter plan with `${__P(threads)}`, a Gatling simulation reading
  `Integer.getInteger("users")`, or a Locust file reading `os.environ.get('CLIENTS')`),
  you can still pass those values via `scriptParams` and the engine will use them. The
  key difference from `Basic` is that Testable does not set up the load management
  framework for you — whatever you pass is what the scenario explicitly reads.

Not applicable to other scenario types (Playwright, Selenium, Node.js, etc.) — omit this field
for non-multi-user scenario types.

scriptParams.description:
JSON string of scenario parameter key/value pairs to pass to the scenario at runtime.
These values are passed to any parameters declared in the scenario's `paramsConfig`
(see the Scenario API). Declaring parameters in the scenario via `paramsConfig` makes it
reusable across many configurations with different values.

**BEST PRACTICE**: Parameterize scenarios by declaring parameters in the scenario's
`paramsConfig`, then supply values here per configuration. This keeps scenarios reusable
and avoids hardcoding environment-specific values (base URLs, credentials, thresholds, etc.).

**FOR LOCUST/JMETER/GATLING SCENARIOS with `loadType: "Basic"`**: Use scriptParams to
control concurrency and duration within each engine. These are the standard parameter names
the scenario should declare and reference:

- **JMeter**: `threads` (virtual users per engine), `duration` (seconds), `rampup` (seconds).
  Reference in JMX via `${__P(threads)}`, `${__P(duration)}`, `${__P(rampup)}`.
  Example: `{"threads": "100", "duration": "300", "rampup": "60"}`

- **Gatling**: `users` (virtual users per engine), `duration` (seconds).
  Reference in Scala via `Integer.getInteger("users")`, `Integer.getInteger("duration")`.
  Example: `{"users": "50", "duration": "180"}`

- **Locust**: `clients` (virtual users per engine), `runtime` (e.g., "5m"), `spawn-rate`.
  These are passed as command line args (--users, --runtime, --spawn-rate).
  Example: `{"clients": "75", "runtime": "300", "spawn-rate": "10"}`

For any scenario type, additional custom parameters your scenario expects can also be passed
here (e.g., `{"baseUrl": "https://api.example.com", "timeout": "30"}`).

imageDiffMode.description: Image comparison mode for scenarios that support screenshot capture

tools.name: updateOrg
tools.description:
[write] PUT /org-details — Updates the organization associated with the current credentials. Both `PUT` and `PATCH`
are supported and behave identically. All fields are optional; only the fields included
in the request body are updated.

**What Can Be Updated:**

- `name` — Display name of the organization
- `email` — Primary contact email for the organization
- `settings` — The main configuration map (see `OrgSettings` schema for all properties)
- `notifications` — Organization-level default notification channels
- `dashboardId` — ID of the default test results dashboard
- `dashboardFunctionalId` — ID of the default functional test dashboard
- `features` — Feature flags string (admin use only)

**Who Calls This Endpoint?**
The account settings page (`account-settings` component) calls this endpoint with the full
`settings` object when the user clicks "Save Settings". Display-preference changes (sort,
filter, groupBy) in the test cases list also call this endpoint to persist view state.

**Region Sync Behavior:**
If the org has a `region` setting (smoke test region) that matches the monitoring
`defaultRegion`, updating either one will automatically sync the other to keep them
in agreement.

**Encryption Key Management:**
If the `encryptionSource` or `encryptionKey` in `settings` changes, all existing
data encryption keys for the organization are automatically deleted and must be
regenerated.
 Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

name.description: New display name for the organization.

email.description: New primary contact email for the organization.

dashboardId.description:
ID of the dashboard to use as the default results view for load tests.
Set to `null` to use the system default dashboard.

dashboardFunctionalId.description:
ID of the dashboard to use as the default results view for functional tests.
Set to `null` to use the system default dashboard.

settings.description:
Organization-wide configuration settings. All values are optional. Settings are stored
as a flat key-value map where boolean flags are stored as the strings `"true"` or `"false"`,
and file contents are stored as base64-encoded strings.

Settings are grouped into the following categories:

**Display Preferences** — persisted UI state for the test cases list and test case detail view.

**Test Runner** — default cloud region, provider, and instance type settings used when creating new tests.

**Cloud Providers** — which cloud providers and regions are enabled for test execution.

**Cleanup / Retention** — automated test result cleanup and retention policies.

**Test Execution Defaults** — distributed traces, failure capture, and output limits.

**Package Manager / Tools** — custom npmrc, pip, Maven, OpenFin, and Playwright configuration.

**Browser Cleanup** — automated Chrome/Chromium profile cleanup thresholds.

**Encryption** — cloud KMS provider and key used to encrypt sensitive test data at rest.

**Email Notifications** — which content sections to include in test result email reports.

**Billing** — cost optimization strategy and category priority order.

**AI** — custom AI API keys for AI-assisted test generation and analysis.

**Resource Naming** — how URL request paths are grouped into named resources for reporting.

**Network** — global environment variables and network proxy settings.

**Access Limits** — per-org limits on concurrent agents, output files, logging, and source code capture.

sort.description:
Default sort order for the test executions list. Persisted when the user changes the
sort order on the test cases page.
Common values: `lastRun` (most recently run first), `name` (alphabetical), `status`.

filter.description:
Default status filter for the test executions list. Stored as the `id` of the selected
filter option. Common values: `all`, `failed`, `passed`, `running`.

groupBy.description:
Default grouping mode for the test executions list.
Common values: `scenario` (by script type), `tag`, `none`. Default: `scenario`.

layout.description:
Display layout for the test cases list. Values: `minimal` (compact rows) or `card`
(expanded card view). Default: `minimal`.

showActiveTestTraffic.description:
`"true"` to show a live traffic chart on the test cases page for running tests.
Default: `"true"`.

tcGroupBy.description:
Default grouping mode on the test case detail page (test configurations list).
Common values: `scenario`, `tag`, `none`. Default: `scenario`.

tcLayout.description:
Display layout on the test case detail page. Values: `minimal` or `card`.
Default: `minimal`.

tcSort.description: Default sort order on the test case detail page. Default: `lastRun`.

tcFilter.description: Default status filter on the test case detail page. Stored as the filter option ID.

defaultRegionType.description:
Specifies how the default test runner region is identified:
- `existing` — use a pre-configured region by its numeric ID (stored in `defaultRegion`)
- `new` — use a provider-supplied region by name (stored in `defaultRegion` as a region name string)

defaultRegion.description:
The default region for test execution. Interpretation depends on `defaultRegionType`:
- If `existing`: the numeric ID of a pre-existing region (e.g., `"1"`)
- If `new`: the region name as returned by the provider (e.g., `"us-east-1"`)

defaultProviderId.description:
The numeric ID of the default cloud provider, stored as a string.
Used when `defaultRegionType` is `new` to identify the provider supplying the region.

region.description:
Legacy smoke test region ID, stored as a string. Used to pre-select the region
for one-click smoke tests. Default: `"1"`. Synced with the monitoring
`defaultRegion` when both are set to the same value.

standardTestRunner.description:
When `true` (default), tests use the standard shared test runners. When `false`,
org-specific test runner configuration (`testRunnerSettings` or advanced instance
type settings) is used.

testRunnerSettings.description:
Custom test runner configuration used when `standardTestRunner=false` and the runner
type is set to "Basic". This is a free-form object whose structure depends on the
provider configuration. Only used when `standardTestRunner` is `false`.

awsAdvancedInstanceType.description:
AWS EC2 instance type for advanced (non-standard) AWS test runners.
Only used when `standardTestRunner=false` and the runner type is "Advanced".
Example: `"c5.2xlarge"`.

azureAdvancedInstanceType.description:
Azure VM size for advanced Azure test runners.
Only used when `standardTestRunner=false` and the runner type is "Advanced".
Example: `"Standard_D4s_v3"`.

gcpAdvancedInstanceType.description:
GCP machine type for advanced GCP test runners.
Only used when `standardTestRunner=false` and the runner type is "Advanced".
Example: `"n1-standard-4"`.

defaultRegion:spot.description:
`"true"` to use spot/preemptible instances for the default test region.
Only applicable for private AWS/GCP providers.

defaultRegion:vpc.description:
AWS VPC ID to launch test runners in for the default region.
Only applicable when the default provider is AWS.

defaultRegion:subnet.description:
AWS subnet ID or `"any"` for automatic subnet selection in the default region.
Also used for Azure subnet. Only applicable for AWS/Azure providers.

defaultRegion:keyPair.description:
AWS EC2 key pair name for SSH access to test runners in the default region.
Only applicable for AWS providers.

defaultRegion:elasticIps.description:
Elastic IP allocation for test runners. Value is either `"any"` (use any available
elastic IP from the pool) or a comma-separated list of specific IP addresses.
Only applicable for AWS providers.

defaultRegion:forceAssociateElasticIps.description:
`"true"` to force-associate elastic IPs even if the instance already has a public IP.
Only applicable for AWS providers.

defaultRegion:resourceGroup.description:
Azure resource group name for test runners in the default region.
Only applicable for Azure providers.

defaultRegion:network.description: Azure VNet name or GCP network name for test runners in the default region.

defaultRegion:gcpNetwork.description:
GCP VPC network name for test runners in the default region.
Only applicable for GCP providers.

defaultRegion:gcpSubNetwork.description:
GCP subnetwork name for test runners in the default region.
Only applicable for GCP providers.

defaultRegion:gcpZone.description:
GCP zone name or `"any"` for automatic zone selection in the default region.
Only applicable for GCP providers.

isAwsEnabled.description:
`"true"` if AWS cloud provider is enabled for this organization.
Controls whether AWS regions appear as test runner options.

isAzureEnabled.description: `"true"` if Azure cloud provider is enabled for this organization.

isGcpEnabled.description: `"true"` if Google Cloud provider is enabled for this organization.

isAwsEnabledAllRegions.description:
`"true"` if all available AWS regions are enabled. When `"false"`, only the regions
listed in `awsRegionsSelected` are available.

isAzureEnabledAllRegions.description:
`"true"` if all available Azure regions are enabled. When `"false"`, only the regions
listed in `azureRegionsSelected` are available.

isGcpEnabledAllRegions.description:
`"true"` if all available GCP regions are enabled. When `"false"`, only the regions
listed in `gcpRegionsSelected` are available.

awsRegionsSelected.description:
Comma-separated list of AWS region names that are available to this organization.
Only applicable when `isAwsEnabledAllRegions` is `"false"`.

azureRegionsSelected.description:
Comma-separated list of Azure region names that are available to this organization.
Only applicable when `isAzureEnabledAllRegions` is `"false"`.

gcpRegionsSelected.description:
Comma-separated list of GCP region names that are available to this organization.
Only applicable when `isGcpEnabledAllRegions` is `"false"`.

cleanupPolicy.description:
Automated cleanup policy for old test execution results.
- `AfterEach` — delete old results after each new execution, keeping only `retentionCount`
- `Periodic` — run cleanup on a schedule

retentionCount.description:
Number of test execution results to retain per test configuration when
`cleanupPolicy` is `AfterEach`. Older results beyond this count are deleted.
Stored as a string number.

tracesEnabled.description:
`"true"` to capture distributed trace data (OpenTelemetry/Jaeger) for test runs.
Default: `"true"`. When disabled, `onlyCaptureFailure` has no effect.

onlyCaptureFailure.description:
`"true"` to only capture trace/screenshot data when a test step fails.
Reduces storage usage for large test suites. Only applies when `tracesEnabled` is `"true"`.

reassignOnFail.description:
`"true"` to automatically reassign (re-queue) a test case to a new agent when a
test run fails due to an infrastructure error (not a test assertion failure).

reassignOnFailFunctional.description:
`"true"` to automatically reassign functional test cases on failure. Mirrors
`reassignOnFail` but applies only to functional test types.

percentiles.description:
Comma-separated list of percentile values to compute and display in test result
reports. Applies to all timing metrics (response time, connect time, etc.).
Default: `"50,75,90,95,99"`.

limitAllowOutputFiles.description:
`"true"` to allow test runners to capture and upload output files (e.g., downloaded
files, generated reports). Set to `"false"` to prohibit file uploads. Default: `"true"`.

limitAllowLogging.description:
`"true"` to allow test runners to capture and upload log output. Set to `"false"` to
prohibit log capture. Default: `"true"`.

limitAllowSourceCode.description:
`"true"` to allow test source code to be included in test result artifacts.
Set to `"false"` to prevent source code from being stored. Default: `"true"`.

freeAgentsOnly.description:
`"true"` to restrict test execution to free/self-hosted agents only, preventing
use of paid cloud test runners. Useful for on-prem deployments or cost control.

maxAgents.description:
Maximum number of concurrent test runner agents allowed for this organization.
Use `"All"` to allow unlimited agents, or a numeric string (e.g., `"10"`) to cap
concurrent usage.

selfHostedOnly.description:
`"true"` to restrict all tests to self-hosted (on-prem) runners only.
Only applicable in self-hosted deployments.

globalEnv.description:
Global environment variables injected into every test execution for this organization.
Key-value pairs where both keys and values are strings. Variables defined here can be
overridden at the test configuration level.

hasCustomNpmrc.description:
`"true"` if a custom `.npmrc` configuration file is set for this organization.
When `"true"`, `customNpmrc` must also be set.

customNpmrc.description:
Base64-encoded content of a custom `.npmrc` file. Used to configure private npm
registries or authentication for Node.js-based tests.
Default content (unencoded): `registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`.

hasPipSettings.description:
`"true"` if custom pip configuration (pip.conf or requirements extra index URLs)
is set for this organization. When `"true"`, `pipSettings` must also be set.

pipSettings.description:
Base64-encoded content of a custom pip configuration file (`pip.conf`).
Used to configure private PyPI mirrors or authentication for Python-based tests.

hasCustomOpenFin.description:
`"true"` if a custom OpenFin configuration is set for this organization.
When `"true"`, `openFinSettings` must also be set.

openFinSettings.description: Base64-encoded OpenFin configuration content for OpenFin-based test scenarios.

hasMvnSettings.description:
`"true"` if a custom Maven `settings.xml` is configured for this organization.
When `"true"`, `mvnSettings` must also be set.

mvnSettings.description:
Base64-encoded content of a custom Maven `settings.xml` file. Used to configure
private Maven repositories or authentication for Java-based tests.

hasPlaywrightSettings.description:
`"true"` if a custom Playwright download host is configured. When `"true"`,
`playwrightDownloadHost` must also be set.

playwrightDownloadHost.description:
Base64-encoded URL of a custom Playwright browser download host. Used in
air-gapped or private environments where browsers cannot be downloaded from
the public Playwright CDN.

jmeterPluginRepos.description:
Semicolon-separated list of JMeter plugin repository URLs. Added to the plugin
manager configuration so test runners can install plugins from these sources.
Default (public): `https://jmeter-plugins.org/repo/`.

hostsFile.description:
Base64-encoded content of a custom `/etc/hosts` file. Injected into all test runner
containers to override DNS resolution. Useful for mapping hostnames to private IPs
in test environments.

hostAliasesFile.description:
Base64-encoded content of a host aliases file. Similar to `hostsFile` but used for
Kubernetes-style host aliases, mapping additional hostnames to existing IPs.

disableNetworkRequestProxy.description:
`"true"` to disable the Testable network request proxy for this organization's tests.
The proxy is used for request capture and reporting. Disabling it may reduce overhead
but will limit network-level visibility in results.

resourceParts.description:
Number of URL path segments used to group HTTP requests into named resources for
the resource-level breakdown in test reports. For example, with `resourceParts=2`,
the URL `/api/users/123/profile` would be grouped under `/api/users`.
Default: `2`.

resourceNameIgnoreNonMatch.description:
When `true`, HTTP requests whose URLs do not match any `resourceNameMappings` pattern
are excluded from the resource breakdown rather than shown with their raw URL path.

resourceNameMappings.description:
Ordered list of resource name mapping rules. Each rule maps a URL/resource pattern
(regular expression) to a display name for grouping requests in resource breakdown
reports. Applied in order; the first matching rule wins. When empty or omitted,
only the path-parts logic (see `resourceParts`) is used.

**Encoding:** If a user asks for resource name mappings or provides them, assume
each rule's `pattern` and `result` are base64-encoded on the wire; decode for display,
encode when submitting.

id.description: Unique identifier for this mapping (e.g. UUID). Used by the UI to track and reorder rules.

pattern.description:
**Base64-encoded** regular expression pattern. When decoded, it is matched against the
resource identifier string (e.g. `GET https://api.example.com/users/123/profile`).
Use standard regex syntax; named capture groups (e.g. `(?<symbol>.*)`) can be referenced
in `result` as `${symbol}`.

result.description:
**Base64-encoded** replacement string. When decoded, this is the resource name to use
when the pattern matches. May contain placeholders like `${namedGroup}` that are
replaced with the corresponding regex named group from the pattern.

browserCleanupDuration.description:
Cleanup browser profile data (cookies, cache, local storage) after this duration.
Format: `{number}{unit}` where unit is `h` (hours), `d` (days), or `m` (months).
For example, `"7d"` cleans up browser data older than 7 days.
Mutually exclusive with `browserCleanupDiskUsage`.

browserCleanupDiskUsage.description:
Trigger browser profile cleanup when disk usage by browser data exceeds this
percentage (0–100). For example, `90` triggers cleanup when disk is 90% full.
Mutually exclusive with `browserCleanupDuration`.

encryptionSource.description:
The numeric ID (as a string) of the cloud provider used for KMS key management.
The provider must be an AWS, Azure, or GCP private provider configured for this org.
When set, test data is encrypted at rest using the specified KMS key.
Set to `null` or omit to disable org-specific encryption.

encryptionSourceDisabled.description:
`"true"` if encryption has been explicitly disabled for this organization
(overriding any system-level encryption default).

encryptionKey.description:
The KMS key identifier for encrypting test data. Format depends on the cloud provider:
- **AWS**: ARN of the KMS key (e.g., `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abc-123`)
- **Azure**: `{keyVaultResourceId}|{keyName}`
- **GCP**: `{keyRing}|{cryptoKey}`
Must be set when `encryptionSource` is set.

emailNotificationAssertions.description:
`"true"` to include assertion pass/fail details in test result email notifications.
Default: `"true"`.

emailNotificationSuccess.description:
`"true"` to send email notifications when tests pass (in addition to failures).
Default: `"true"`.

emailNotificationImages.description:
`"true"` to include screenshots and chart images in test result email notifications.
Default: `"true"`.

emailNotificationLogging.description:
`"true"` to include log output excerpts in test result email notifications.
Default: `"true"`.

billingStrategy.description:
Cost optimization strategy for selecting test runner instances:
- `MinimizeCost` (default) — always choose the lowest-cost available option
- `MaximizeSpeed` — always choose the fastest available option regardless of cost
- `AsapByCategory` — use `billingChosenCategories` to prioritize by category

billingAsapStrategy.description:
Sub-strategy used when `billingStrategy` is `AsapByCategory` or when minimizing cost
within a category:
- `cheapest` (default) — select the cheapest option within the chosen category
- `fastest` — select the fastest option within the chosen category
- `balanced` — balance cost and speed

billingChosenCategories.description:
Comma-separated ordered list of billing categories to try when `billingStrategy` is
`AsapByCategory`. The system tries each category in order and uses the first one that
has available capacity.
Common values: `TestRunner` (dedicated test runners), `Cloud` (on-demand cloud),
`Shared` (shared pool).

ai.description:
AI-related configuration for this organization. Used to supply custom API keys
for AI-powered test generation and analysis features.

useMyKeys.description:
When `true`, use the organization's own AI API keys instead of the system-provided
keys. When `false`, AI features use the platform's shared API keys (subject to
rate limits).

openai.description:
OpenAI API key for GPT-based test generation and analysis features.
Only used when `useMyKeys` is `true`.

notifications.description:
Replace the organization's notification channels. If provided, the existing
notification list is completely replaced with this array.

notificationMedium.description:
Channel type. `Email`, `Text`, `Voice`, `WhatsApp` for messaging; `HTTP` for webhooks;
`Slack`, `Teams`, `SNS` when those integrations are enabled for the org.

successNotificationStyle.description: When to send a notification on success. `First` = first success only; `Always` = every success; `None` = never.

failureNotificationStyle.description: When to send a notification on failure. `First` = first failure only; `Always` = every failure; `None` = never.

failureNotificationConsecutiveTimes.description: Number of consecutive failures before sending (when failure style is First).

notificationTarget.description:
For Email medium only: `OrgEmail` uses the org's default email; `CustomList` uses
`customNotificationList` (or org default if empty).

customNotificationList.description:
Destination for this channel. Email address for Email; Slack channel or webhook URL for
Slack; Teams channel ID or webhook for Teams; URL for HTTP; SNS topic etc. Optional for
OrgEmail; required for CustomList when the medium needs a target.

tools.name: getCloudMetadata
tools.description:
[write] POST /cloud/metadata — Single wrapper endpoint for discovering cloud-specific metadata needed to configure
OnDemand (*Per Check*) runner sources. This intentionally wraps the AWS, Azure, and GCP
metadata lookups used by the web UI so MCP clients get one tool instead of many.

**AI workflow for creating/updating PerCheck monitor regions:**
1. Call `GET /providers?providerType=OnDemand&down=true` to choose a Test Runner Source.
2. Call this endpoint with `requestType=Regions` or inspect the provider locations to choose

[write] DELETE /providers/:id — Removes a private test runner source (cloud account). Corresponds to the guide
**Management → Delete Test Runner Source**. The source will no longer appear in lists or
be available for new test configurations; existing configurations using it must be updated
to a different test runner source.

**Effects:**
- Test runner source is marked `active=false` (soft delete)
- Organization encryption keys for this source are deleted
- Its regions become unavailable for new test runs
- Returns `204 No Content` if the source is not found

tools.description:
[write] PUT /regions/:id — Updates a region's active state. The primary use case is deactivating a region that is
no longer available or should not receive new test runs (e.g., when decommissioning
an agent pool). Both `PUT` and `PATCH` are supported.

Only regions belonging to private test runner sources (OnDemand) owned by the user's
organization can be updated.

tools.name: deleteExecution
tools.description:
[write] DELETE /executions/:executionId — Permanently deletes a completed test execution and all associated results, including:
- Raw result data
- Aggregated metrics
- Output files (screenshots, logs, etc.)
- Trace data
- Suite/assertion results

**Important Notes:**
- Only works for completed executions (must have `completed: true`)
- If test is still running, stop it first using PUT /executions/:id/stop
- After stopping, wait for completion before deleting
- This operation cannot be undone
- Baseline references to this execution will be removed

**Use Cases:** Clean up failed test runs; Remove test data to free up storage; Comply with data retention policies

- Group related test runs together
- Mark tests with build numbers or commit SHAs
- Associate tests with features, sprints, or releases
- Enable filtering in the UI and API search endpoints

**Tag Naming:**
- Tags are case-sensitive
- Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores
- Maximum length varies by plan
- Duplicate tags on same execution are ignored

**Common Patterns:**
- CI/CD: Tag with build number, branch name, commit SHA
- Release tracking: Tag with release version
- Feature testing: Tag with feature name or ticket ID
- Environment: Tag with env name (dev, staging, prod)

- `Outcome[success] > 98%` - More than 98% of requests successful
- `firstReceivedMs[p95] < 1000` - 95th percentile response time under 1 second
- `bandwidth > 1000000` - Total bandwidth exceeded 1MB

**KPI Types:**
- `value`: Compare metric value/percentile against threshold
- `baseline`: Compare against previous baseline execution

**Use Cases:** CI/CD pass/fail criteria; Automated regression detection; SLA validation; Performance gating

tools.name: startExecution
tools.description:
[write] POST /test-confs/:confId/executions — Creates a new test execution from the specified configuration. By default the test
starts immediately; no further operations are needed.

**Before starting a full execution:** For new or updated scenarios, run a smoke test first
using the `run_smoke_test` tool (with the scenario's script ID). Verify the smoke test
result: `passed` should be `true`, `status` should be `"finished"`, and review `diagnostics`,
`logs`, and `suiteResults` for errors or failed assertions. Treat `passed=false`, log errors,
failed suite tests, or empty suite results with no result events as a failed smoke test to debug
before proceeding. Only start a full test execution once the smoke test looks good.

**When to use (default, no manual_start):**
- Test runs right away. Response has `manualStart: false`.
- Runners are provisioned and the test starts. Poll GET /executions/:id for progress.
- **Note:** `running` may be `false` briefly while infrastructure starts—this is normal.
Do not call requestExecutionStart or manualStartExecution; the test is already starting.

**When to use (manual_start: true in request body):**
- Only provisions infrastructure (on-demand runners); test does not run yet.
- Response has `manualStart: true`. Call PUT /executions/:id/manual-start (manualStartExecution)
to actually start the test when ready.

**Execution flow (default):**
1. Execution record created
2. Test runners allocated (if using on-demand)
3. Test starts running (unless manual_start is specified)
4. Results streamed back during execution
5. Final aggregation and cleanup after completion

**Common patterns:** CI/CD trigger, scheduled run, on-demand API, trigger conditions.

tools.description:
[write] PUT /executions/:executionId/start — Starts an execution that was created with `manual_start: true` (provisioned but not yet running).
Use this when you previously created an execution with manual_start so that infrastructure
was allocated but the test was not started. After this call, the test runs; no need to
call manualStartExecution (that is an alternative endpoint for the same outcome).

**Do not use** for executions created without manual_start—those already start automatically;
`running: false` initially is normal while infrastructure starts.

**Use cases:**
- Start execution created with delayed/manual start
- Coordinate test start across systems
- Start after custom setup/validation

tools.name: manualStartExecution
tools.description:
[write] PUT /executions/:executionId/manual-start — Starts a test execution that was created with `manual_start: true`. Those executions
provision and initialize test runners but do not run until this (or the start) endpoint
is called. Call this when you are ready to actually run the test; runners are already
allocated so load starts quickly.

**Flow:** Create execution with manual_start=true → response has `manualStart: true` →
call this endpoint (or PUT .../start) to kick off the test. Do not call this for
executions created without manual_start; they start automatically.

**Benefits:**
- Precise test start timing
- No delay waiting for runner allocation
- Useful for coordinated testing across systems

tools.name: stopExecution

[write] PUT /executions/:executionId/stop — Requests to stop a running execution before it completes naturally.
Once stopped, the execution will transition through cleanup and result aggregation
before reaching `completed: true` status.

**Process:**
1. Stop signal sent to all test runners
2. Current iterations allowed to complete
3. Results collected and aggregated
4. Resources cleaned up
5. Execution marked as completed

**Important:**
- Don't immediately try to delete after stopping
- Wait for `completed: true` before deletion
- Partial results will still be available
- Test marked as cancelled but results are valid up to stop point

- Extension applies to all test runners
- Works with both duration-based and iteration-based tests

[write] POST /internal/browser — Launch a new browser session on a test runner and return a sessionId for subsequent operations.

When a user asks to inspect, explore, look at, browse, or understand a web app or
OpenFin app as part of generating or updating a scenario, use this tool proactively.
Do not wait for a second prompt that explicitly says to launch a browser. Inspect the
running app with navigation, screenshots, content/title, page listing, page switching,
and evaluate calls as needed, then use those observations to build the scenario.

Two connection modes are supported (controlled by the `connectionMode` parameter):

  • "playwright" (default) — the Testable agent starts a browser and exposes it via
    Playwright's own server protocol. Playwright connects using BrowserType.connect()
    over the `/playwright` WebSocket endpoint. Supports all browser types (chrome,
    firefox, webkit) and the full Playwright API. Use this for standard web automation.

  • "cdp" — the Testable agent exposes a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint and
    Playwright connects using BrowserType.connectOverCDP() over the `/cdp` WebSocket
    endpoint. Chromium/Chrome only. Use this for OpenFin desktop apps or other
    Chromium-based native runtimes. Passing `openfinConfigUrl` automatically forces
    this mode — you do NOT need to set connectionMode="cdp" explicitly in that case.

OpenFin manifest from that URL, launches the OpenFin desktop application (OpenFin is a
thin Chromium wrapper), and then connects to the running app via CDP. The AI does not
need to navigate to any URL — OpenFin opens its own window on launch.

Example flow (standard web):
1. browser_launch(browserName="chrome") -> returns sessionId
2. browser_navigate(sessionId="...", url="https://example.com")
3. browser_screenshot(sessionId="...") -> returns base64 PNG
4. browser_close(sessionId="...")

Example flow (OpenFin):
1. browser_launch(openfinConfigUrl="https://example.com/app.json") -> returns sessionId
   (agent launches the OpenFin app and connects via CDP automatically)
2. browser_screenshot(sessionId="...") -> capture whatever OpenFin opened
3. browser_close(sessionId="...") Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

tools.name: createScenario
tools.description:
[write] POST /scenarios — Creates a new scenario (script) that can be used for load testing or as a custom monitoring script.

This endpoint supports creating scenarios for multiple testing frameworks and scenario types.
The request must be sent as `multipart/form-data` to support file uploads.

See the [Testable Simple API documentation](https://docs.testable.io/api/simple.html) for detailed 
examples and additional guidance for each scenario type.

If your scenario contains code, it's best to confirm with the user that the code contents look correct before proceeding to create the scenario. Exception: when the user asked to create a monitor and the scenario is needed for that monitor, do not pause for code review; create the scenario, smoke test it, fix issues, rerun the smoke test, and then create the monitor.

**Proactive app inspection for scenario generation:**
If the user asks you to inspect, explore, look at, browse, or understand a browser app while generating this
scenario, launch a browser session with the browser tools before finalizing the scenario. Use
`browser_launch`, `browser_navigate`, screenshots, content/title inspection, and targeted evaluation to learn
the real page structure, selectors, timing, titles, messages, and failure states. If the app is OpenFin, launch
with `browser_launch(openfinConfigUrl=...)`, then use `browser_pages`, `browser_switch_page`, screenshots,
content/title inspection, and evaluation to inspect the OpenFin windows. Do not wait for the user to separately
say "launch the browser" when they already asked you to inspect or explore the app as part of scenario creation.

**CRITICAL — no placeholder scenarios:**
Do not call this endpoint with placeholder, dummy, or empty script contents. Never use values like
`scriptId=0`, `scenario_name=dummy`, `name=dummy`, or base64 for the string `dummy` just to create an
empty scenario shell. A scenario must be created with the real runnable script, uploaded files, repository
configuration, or `ai_instructions` needed to satisfy the user's request. If you do not have enough
information to write or generate the actual scenario, ask the user for the missing details before calling
createScenario.

**Monitoring browser-check workflow:**
When the user asks to create a monitor that loads a page in a browser, checks the page title/content, clicks
through a flow, accepts cookies, checks links, takes a screenshot, or otherwise uses browser automation, create
a real Playwright scenario first (usually `scenario_type=Playwright`, `playwright_runstyle=library`,
`framework=Mocha`, with a runnable `playwright_script` and required `package.json`). Do not create
`scenario_type=AI` and do not provide `ai_instructions` for ordinary browser monitors unless the user explicitly
asks for an AI-generated/self-healing AI scenario. Then run `run_smoke_test` with the returned scenario ID,
inspect `passed`, `diagnostics`, `status`, `logs`, `suiteResults`, and `suiteTestResults`, fix scenario script/configuration issues,
and rerun smoke tests until the scenario passes or a real external blocker prevents progress. After the smoke
test passes, create a Custom monitor using the returned scenario ID as `customScenarioId`. Do not create an
empty or dummy scenario first. Do not ask the user whether to continue between scenario creation, smoke
testing, fixing, rerunning, and monitor creation. Do not stop after creating the scenario or after a failed
smoke test and tell the user that monitor creation or fixing is a next step; immediately continue through the
full monitor workflow in the same user request unless a tool error or missing required detail blocks you.
Treat `passed=false`, `diagnostics.reasons`, error/fatal log lines, failed suite tests, or a finished smoke
test with empty `suiteResults` and no result events as a failed smoke test that needs debugging.

**After creating a scenario:** Run a smoke test using the `run_smoke_test` tool with the new scenario's script ID (returned in the response). Verify the smoke test result: check that `passed` is `true`, `status` is `"finished"`, and review `diagnostics`, `logs`, `suiteResults`, `suiteTestResults`, result events, and assertions for errors or failed tests. Treat `passed=false`, `diagnostics.reasons`, error/fatal log lines, failed suite tests/assertions, or a finished smoke test with empty `suiteResults` and no result events as a failed smoke test. Fix scenario script/configuration issues and rerun smoke tests until the scenario passes or a real external blocker prevents progress. Only after the smoke test looks good should you start a full test execution or report that the scenario is ready.

## Scenario Types

The `scenario_type` parameter determines which type of scenario to create. Supported values:
- `Code` - Node.js script
- `JMeter` - JMeter test plan
- `Gatling` - Gatling simulation
- `Locust` - Locust file
- `Selenium` - Selenium tests (Java, JavaScript, Webdriver.io)
- `Playwright` - Playwright tests (Library or Test Runner)
- `Puppeteer` - Puppeteer script
- `Java` - Java program
- `Postman` - Postman collection
- `Har` - HAR file replay
- `PhantomJs` - PhantomJS/SlimerJS script
- `AI` - AI-generated/self-healing browser test scenario (Playwright). Use only when explicitly requested; do not use for ordinary browser-based monitors.

If `scenario_type` is not specified, it will be auto-detected based on the files and parameters provided.
If `ai_instructions` is provided without an explicit `scenario_type`, the type is automatically set to `AI`; therefore do not provide `ai_instructions` for normal Playwright browser monitor scripts.

**Node.js-based scenarios (testable-utils):** For scenario types Code, Playwright (Node runtime), Puppeteer, Selenium JavaScript, and Webdriver.io, use the testable-utils npm package when the scenario needs metrics, CSV data, barriers, logging, or similar. When you need the full API reference, use make_http_request with method=GET and url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/testable/node-script-utils/refs/heads/master/README.md .

## Common Parameters

These parameters apply to all scenario types:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `scenario_name` | Text | Name for the scenario. Auto-generated if not specified |
| `testcase_folder` | Text | Folder path for the test case this scenario belongs to (e.g., "/MyFolder"). **Must match the folder of the test case.** |
| `testcase_name` | Text | Test case name this scenario belongs to. **The scenario and test configuration must be in the same test case.** |
| `params[*]` | Text | **Declared scenario parameters** — these become part of the scenario definition (`paramsConfig`) and appear automatically in any test configuration that uses this scenario. Each `params[name]=defaultValue` entry declares a parameter named `name` with the given default value. The scenario reads the parameter at runtime as an environment variable (`NAME` uppercased, e.g. `params[apiUrl]` → `API_URL`). For JMeter: `${__P(name)}`; for Gatling: `System.getProperty("name")`; for Locust: env var. Any scenario metadata field that contains `${paramName}` syntax will also have the placeholder replaced with the parameter's value at runtime on the test runner — so parameters can be referenced in scenario settings (e.g. Locust host, argument strings) as well as in script code. **BEST PRACTICE**: Always declare parameters for environment-specific values (base URLs, credentials, user counts, duration) so the scenario is reusable across configurations. **DO NOT use `params[*]` for framework configuration fields** such as `playwright_script`, `framework`, `mocha_timeout`, `puppeteer_script`, `language`, etc. — those are top-level form fields. |
| `params[*].encrypted` | Text | Set to "true" to encrypt a parameter value. Example: `params[apiKey].encrypted=true` |
| `files[*]` | File | Additional files (CSVs, data files, etc.). Use filename attribute to specify path within scenario |
| `platform` | Text | OS platform: `linux` or `win32`. Defaults to linux |
| `java_version` | Text | Java version if applicable: `1.8`, `11`, or `17` |
| `node_version` | Text | Node.js version: `10`, `14`, `18`, or `latest` |
| `additional_setup_command` | Text | Shell command to run before test starts |
| `teardown_command` | Text | Shell command to run after test finishes |
| `root_folder` | Text | Subdirectory to run test from if all project files are in a subdirectory |
| `assertions_exclusion_pattern` | Text | Comma-separated regex patterns to exclude test steps from reporting |

### OpenFin with Puppeteer

To test an OpenFin application with Puppeteer on Testable, use `puppeteer.launch()` with the
`channel` option set to `'openfin:[app-config-file]'`. Testable intercepts this and launches
the OpenFin runtime before connecting Puppeteer to it.

**CRITICAL — CommonJS only for OpenFin Puppeteer:**
When generating an OpenFin + Puppeteer scenario, **always** generate a `package.json` with
`"type": "commonjs"` (and **NOT** `"type": "module"`). Use CommonJS syntax in the test spec file:
`require()` instead of `import`, and `module.exports` if needed. OpenFin with Puppeteer does not
support ES modules in this context.

**CRITICAL — correct launch pattern:**
```javascript
// CORRECT: Use puppeteer.launch() with the channel option
const browser = await puppeteer.launch({ channel: 'openfin:app_sample.json' });

// WRONG: Do NOT use puppeteer.connect() or pass openfinConfigUrl to connect()
// const browser = await puppeteer.connect({ browserWSEndpoint: wsEndpoint, openfinConfigUrl: ... }); // ❌ NEVER DO THIS
```

The `channel` value format is `openfin:[config]` where `[config]` is either:
- A **relative path** to the app config JSON within your uploaded files (e.g., `openfin:app_sample.json`)
- A **remote URL** to the app config JSON (e.g., `openfin:https://example.com/app.json`)

Also set `openfin_config_url` as a scenario parameter to the same config path/URL — this lets
Testable know the scenario uses OpenFin.

**Puppeteer version for OpenFin:**
You must pin the Puppeteer version in `package.json` to match the Chromium version used by the
OpenFin runtime. To determine the correct version:
1. Retrieve the OpenFin config file (from `openfin_config_url` or the uploaded files).
2. Extract the `runtime.version` field from the config (e.g. `31.1.1.21`).
3. Call the **resolve_openfin_version** tool with that version. The tool returns `puppeteerVersion`;
   use that value in `package.json` for the `puppeteer` dependency (e.g. `"puppeteer": "19.8.0"`).
4. If the tool call fails or returns an error, use the placeholder `"${puppeteerVersion}"` as fallback
   (Testable may still resolve it at runtime, but pinning via the tool is preferred when possible).

**Full example script (`test.testable.js`) using Mocha + Chai (CommonJS):**
```javascript
const puppeteer = require('puppeteer');
const { expect } = require('chai');

let browser;

before(async function() {
  // 'openfin:app_sample.json' tells Testable to launch OpenFin using the uploaded app config.
  // Replace app_sample.json with your config file path or a remote https:// URL.
  browser = await puppeteer.launch({ channel: 'openfin:app_sample.json' });
});

describe('OpenFin App', () => {
  it('should load the main window', async () => {
    const pages = await browser.pages();
    expect(pages.length).to.be.greaterThan(0);
    const page = pages[0];
    await page.screenshot({ path: 'screenshot.png' });
    const title = await page.title();
    expect(title).to.not.be.empty;
  });
});

after(async () => {
  if (browser) await browser.close();
});
```

**Example `package.json` for OpenFin Puppeteer (commonjs, pin to matching Puppeteer version, framework=Mocha):**
```json
{
  "name": "openfin-puppeteer-test",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "type": "commonjs",
  "dependencies": {
    "puppeteer": "19.8.0",
    "mocha": "^10.0.0",
    "chai": "^4.3.7"

}
```

appear as OnDemand sources; they appear as regions under the organization's self-hosted
test runner source.

- Response time metrics: firstReceivedMs, connectionOpenMs, connectionCloseMs
