Same as the overall intervals endpoint but scoped to one region.

Useful for:
- Analyzing performance differences across regions
- Debugging region-specific issues
- Comparing regional performance

tools.name: getExecutionResources
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/resources — Retrieves metrics aggregated by resource (URL/endpoint) for the entire execution.
Each resource represents a distinct URL, custom metric namespace, or user-defined
tracking point.

**Load tests only:** Per-resource aggregation is only produced when the execution's
`testType` is `Load` (from the parent test configuration). For `Functional` or
`Monitor` executions this endpoint returns an empty JSON array (`[]`)—that is
expected, not a sign that the run failed or that metrics are missing from the system.
Use execution-level metric endpoints for those test types.

**Resource Examples:**
- `GET https://api.example.com/users` (HTTP request)
- `MyCustomMetric` (Custom metric from test script)
- `Database Query` (Custom tracking point)

**Response Structure:**
- Each resource includes its own summary metrics
- Optionally includes per-interval metrics per resource
- Useful for identifying slow endpoints

**Performance Note:**
Setting `intervals=true` returns a large amount of data. Recommend retrieving intervals
for specific resources using /executions/:id/resources/:resourceId instead.

**Use Cases:** Identify slowest endpoints in your application; Compare performance across different resources; Find which URLs had the most errors

query_intervals.description: Include per-interval metrics for each resource

tools.name: getExecutionRegionResources
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/regions/:region/resources — Retrieves metrics aggregated by resource for a specific execution region.
Same as the overall resources endpoint but scoped to one region.

**Load tests only:** Per-resource aggregation exists only when the execution's
`testType` is `Load`. For `Functional` or `Monitor` executions this returns an
empty JSON array (`[]`).

tools.name: getExecutionResource
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/resources/:resourceId — Retrieves detailed metrics for a single resource (URL/endpoint) including optional
per-interval breakdown.

**Load tests only:** Meaningful per-resource aggregates are produced only when the
execution's `testType` is `Load`. For `Functional` or `Monitor` executions, the
list endpoint `GET /executions/{executionId}/resources` returns `[]`, so there is
normally nothing to look up here—prefer execution-level metrics instead.

**Resource ID:** 
Use GET /executions/:id/resources to get the resource ID first.

**Use Cases:** Analyze performance of specific endpoint over time; Identify when an endpoint started performing poorly; Compare endpoint behavior to overall test performance

tools.name: getExecutionRegionResource
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/regions/:region/resources/:resourceId — Retrieves detailed metrics for a single resource within a specific execution region.

**Load tests only:** Same constraint as `GET /executions/{executionId}/resources/{resourceId}`—per-resource
aggregates apply when `testType` is `Load`. For `Functional` or `Monitor` executions,
`GET .../regions/{region}/resources` returns `[]`; use execution- or region-level metrics instead.

tools.name: getExecutionBuckets
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/buckets — Retrieves histogram bucket details for specified metrics. Histograms group metric values
into buckets/ranges to show distribution.

**Use Cases:** Analyze response time distribution (e.g., how many requests took 0-100ms, 100-200ms, etc.); See distribution of HTTP status codes; Understand metric value spread vs just averages

**Example:**
Get response time distribution: `?metrics=123&granularity=10s`

query_metrics.description: Comma-separated list of metric definition IDs

tools.name: getExecutionBucketIntervals
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/bucket-intervals — Retrieves time-series intervals for requests/results that fell into a specific histogram bucket.

**Use Cases:** Analyze when slow requests occurred (e.g., all requests > 1000ms); Track error rates over time (e.g., HTTP 5xx responses); Identify patterns in specific value ranges

**Required Parameters:**
- `bucket`: Bucket identifier/range
- `metrics`: Metric definition IDs
- `granularity`: Time bucket size

query_metrics.description: Comma-separated list of metric definition IDs

tools.name: getExecutionLogs
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/logs — Retrieves all logging captured during test execution in JSON or text format.
Includes system logs (test lifecycle events) and user-generated logs from test scripts.
Ignore NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED warnings, ExperimentalWarning, and “ignore certificate errors” and do not mention that
in any analysis you return to the user about the logs .

**Default for AI:** Use `limit=1000` unless the user explicitly needs more or all logs.
This keeps responses manageable; use `limit=-1` only when the user asks for the full log set.

**Log Levels:**
- `Error`: Critical errors and failures
- `Info`: Informational messages about test progress
- `Debug`: Detailed debugging information

**When analyzing why an execution failed:** Always use `level=Debug` to capture the most detailed
information about what went wrong. Debug logs include fine-grained trace data, internal state, and
step-by-step execution details that are essential for root cause analysis. Do not use `Error` or
`Info` level when investigating failures — you will miss critical context.

**Format:**
- Without `.txt`: Returns JSON with structured log entries
- With `.txt`: Returns plain text format suitable for download

**Use Cases:** Debug test failures; Monitor test progress in real-time; Extract errors for reporting; Download complete log file for offline analysis

query_limit.description: Number of log entries to return (-1 for all)

query_level.description: Minimum log level to return. Use `Debug` when analyzing why an execution failed — this is the most inclusive level and surfaces all available detail. `Info` omits debug traces; `Error` omits both, leaving only critical failures. Default to `Debug` for any failure investigation unless the user asks for a specific level.

query_since.description: Start timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_until.description: End timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_groups.description: Filter by log group IDs (comma-separated). Not names. Use getExecutionLogGroups to map log group name to id, then pass those ids here.

tools.name: getExecutionLogGroups
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/log-groups — Retrieves information about all log groups (categories) available for this execution.
Log groups organize logs by source/type (e.g., JMeter output, system logs, custom logs).

**Common Log Groups:**
- System logs (test lifecycle events)
- JMeter logs (jmeter.log, JMeter Console)
- Custom logs from test scripts
- Tool-specific logs (Selenium, Playwright, etc.)

tools.name: getExecutionAgents
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/agents — Retrieves information about all test runners (agents) that participated in this execution.
Each agent represents a machine/container that ran part of your load test.

**Agent Information Includes:**
- Agent ID and location
- Number of virtual users/engines assigned
- Region where agent executed
- Execution timing and status

**Use Cases:** Understand test distribution across runners; Debug agent-specific issues; Analyze resource utilization

tools.name: getExecutionChildren
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/children — Retrieves information about child/sub-executions spawned by this parent execution.
Applicable when tests are configured to spawn multiple child tests.

**Use Cases:** Monitor multi-phase test execution; Track spawned tests from triggers; Aggregate metrics across related tests

tools.name: getResult
tools.description:
[read] GET /results/:resultId — Retrieves details of a single raw result record from the execution.
Each result represents one HTTP request, database query, or other tracked operation.

**Result Contents:**
- Timing metrics (response time, connection time, etc.)
- Resource/URL that was accessed
- Success/failure status
- User/iteration that generated it
- Timestamp and region information
- Associated metrics and custom data

**Use Cases:** Debug specific slow/failed requests; Analyze individual result details; Trace specific user behavior

tools.name: getExecutionResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/results — Downloads raw, unaggregated results from the execution in JSON or CSV format.
Each result represents one HTTP request, operation, or tracked event.

**Important Notes:**
- Can return very large datasets
- Use filtering parameters to reduce payload
- CSV format available by adding .csv extension
- Supports pagination via offset/limit

**Filtering Options:**
- `region`: Specific execution region ID
- `resource`: Specific resource ID
- `since`/`until`: Time range in Unix epoch ms
- `filter`: network (HTTP only), all, other
- `metricDefId`: Filter by specific metric
- `userMetrics=true`: Include user-defined metrics
- `offset`/`limit`: Pagination

**Response Headers:**
- `X-Testable-Count`: Total matching results
- `X-Testable-Offset`: Current offset
- `X-Testable-PageLength`: Number of results in response

**Use Cases:** Detailed analysis in external tools; Custom metric analysis; Data science/ML input; Audit trail

query_since.description: Start timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_until.description: End timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_limit.description: Number of results to return (-1 for all)

tools.name: getExecutionSlowestResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/slowest-results — Retrieves the slowest raw results from the execution, sorted by response time.
Only includes network/HTTP results by default.

**Use Cases:** Identify slowest requests for optimization; Find performance outliers; Analyze worst-case performance

**Filtering:**
Same parameters as regular results endpoint (region, resource, since, until)

tools.name: getExecutionFailedResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/failed-results — Retrieves all results that failed (non-successful HTTP status, exceptions, timeouts, etc.).
Available in both JSON and CSV formats.

**Failure Criteria:**
- HTTP 4xx/5xx status codes
- Network timeouts
- Connection errors
- Test script exceptions

**Use Cases:** Debug test failures; Identify error patterns; Generate failure reports

tools.name: getExecutionSlowestIterations
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/slowest-iterations — Retrieves the slowest test iterations, sorted by total iteration duration.
Each iteration represents one complete execution of the test scenario by a virtual user.

**Use Cases:** Find which virtual users had performance issues; Identify slow iteration patterns; Debug performance variability

tools.name: getExecutionThreads
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/threads — Retrieves information about all virtual user threads (execution contexts) in the test.
Each thread represents a unique virtual user session.

**Response:**
Array of thread info including thread ID and number of iterations executed.

**Use Cases:** List all virtual users; See which users executed most iterations; Identify thread-specific issues

tools.name: getThreadIterations
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/threads/:threadId/iterations — Retrieves all iterations executed by a specific virtual user thread.

**Use Cases:** Analyze specific user behavior; Debug user-specific issues; Track iteration timing for one user

tools.name: getIterationResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/iterations/:iterationId/results — Retrieves all results (requests, operations) that occurred during a specific test iteration.
Available in both JSON and CSV formats.

**Use Cases:** Analyze complete iteration execution; Debug slow/failed iteration; Correlate all requests in one user flow

tools.name: getExecutionSessionNums
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/session-nums — Retrieves a list of all unique browser session numbers from the execution.
Only applicable for browser-based tests (Selenium, Playwright, Puppeteer).

**Use Cases:** List all browser sessions; Filter output files by session; Correlate results with browser instances

tools.name: getExecutionTraces
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/traces — Retrieves all connection traces captured during execution. Traces provide detailed
information about individual connections including request/response headers, timing,
and packet-level details.

**Trace Contents:**
- HTTP request/response details
- Timing breakdown (DNS, connect, first byte, etc.)
- Status codes and response sizes
- Optional packet-level data

**Use Cases:** Debug connection issues; Analyze request/response details; Verify headers and payloads

tools.name: getExecutionTrace
tools.description:
[read] GET /execution-traces/:traceId — Retrieves complete details of a single trace including all packets, timing metrics,
and request/response data.

**Packet Data:**
All packet data is base64 encoded. Decode using atob() in JavaScript or
equivalent in other languages.

**Use Cases:** Deep dive into connection details; Debug request/response issues; Verify packet-level behavior

tools.name: getTracePackets
tools.description:
[read] GET /execution-traces/:traceId/packets — Retrieves all packets for a specific trace. Packets represent individual data
exchanges during the connection (DNS lookup, connection open, data sent/received, etc.).

**Packet Types:**
- DnsLookup: DNS resolution
- ConnectionOpened: TCP connection established
- DataSent: Request data sent
- DataReceived: Response data received
- ConnectionClosed: Connection terminated

tools.name: getOutputFileMetadata
tools.description:
[read] GET /output-files/:fileId — Retrieves metadata about a single output file without downloading the actual file.

**Metadata Includes:**
- File name, type, and size
- Capture timestamp
- Associated execution, region, user, iteration
- URLs for viewing/downloading
- Thumbnail URL for images
- Visual diff information if applicable

**Use Cases:** List file details; Verify file availability; Get download URLs

tools.name: viewOutputFile
tools.description:
[read] GET /output-files/:fileId/view — Serves an output file for inline viewing in browser (not as download).
Useful for images, text files, and other viewable content.

query_diff.description: View visual diff overlay for images

tools.name: getOutputFileThumbnail
tools.description:
[read] GET /output-files/:fileId/thumbnail — Retrieves a thumbnail version of an image output file.
Only works for image files.

tools.name: getExecutionOutputFiles
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/output-files — Retrieves metadata for all output files captured during test execution.
Does not download the files themselves - use /output-files/:id/download for that.

**File Types:**
- Screenshots (PNG, JPEG)
- Videos (MP4, WebM)
- HAR files (network recordings)
- Custom files uploaded from test scripts
- Log files
- Performance traces

**Extensive Filtering Options:**
- `since`/`until`: Time range
- `contentType`: Filter by MIME type (e.g., "image/png")
- `agent`: Comma-separated test runner IDs
- `regions`: Comma-separated execution region IDs
- `client`: Global user number (starts at 0)
- `iteration`: Iteration number (starts at 0)
- `failuresOnly=false`: Only files from failed iterations
- `offset`/`limit`: Pagination

**Use Cases:** List all screenshots; Find files from specific user/iteration; Get files captured during failures; Build custom file browser

query_since.description: Start timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_until.description: End timestamp in Unix epoch milliseconds

query_regions.description: Comma-separated list of execution region IDs

query_failuresOnly.description: Only return files from failed iterations

tools.name: getIterationOutputFiles
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/iterations/:iterationId/output-files — Retrieves metadata for all output files captured during a specific test iteration.

**Use Cases:** Get all screenshots from one iteration; Correlate files with iteration behavior; Debug specific iteration issues

tools.name: getSuiteResult
tools.description:
[read] GET /suite-results/:resultId — Retrieves detailed information about a single suite result (test assertion execution).

**Suite Result Contents:**
- Suite metadata (name, timing)
- Individual test steps and their results
- Error information if failed
- Screenshots captured during suite
- Correlation with iteration/user

**Use Cases:** Debug failed assertions; Analyze test step timing; View complete assertion hierarchy

tools.name: getSuiteTestResult
tools.description:
[read] GET /suite-test-results/:testResultId — Retrieves detailed information about a single test step result within a suite.

**Test Result Contents:**
- Test step name and state (passed, failed, retried)
- Timing information
- Error details if failed
- Parent suite information
- Child test steps if any

tools.name: getSuiteTestResultChildren
tools.description:
[read] GET /suite-test-results/:testResultId/child-results — Retrieves all child test step results for a given test step.
Test steps can be hierarchical with parent/child relationships.

**Use Cases:** Navigate test step hierarchy; View nested test structure; Analyze multi-level test flows

tools.name: getExecutionSuiteResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-results — Retrieves all suite/assertion results from the execution in JSON or CSV format.
Includes all test suites and their test steps with pass/fail status.

**Filtering:**
- `region`: Filter by execution region
- `since`/`until`: Time range filter
- `offset`/`limit`: Pagination

**CSV Export:**
Add .csv extension for CSV format with all suite and test step results.

**Use Cases:** Export all test assertions; Analyze test pass rates; Generate test reports

tools.name: getExecutionSuiteSummaries
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-summaries — Retrieves aggregated summary statistics for all test suites in the execution.
Groups results by suite and provides pass/fail counts, timing stats, and error counts.

**Summary Metrics:**
- Tests passed/failed/retried
- Average/min/max duration
- Screenshot count
- Error summaries

**CSV Export:**
Add .csv extension and optionally set `includeErrors=true` to include error details.

**Use Cases:** High-level test pass/fail overview; Compare suite performance; Identify problematic test suites

tools.name: getExecutionSuiteErrors
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-errors — Retrieves a summary of all errors encountered during test suite execution,
aggregated by error type with occurrence counts.

**Use Cases:** Identify most common errors; Prioritize bug fixes; Track error patterns

tools.name: getExecutionSuiteRelated
tools.description: [read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-related — Retrieves related information for suite results including browsers, errors, and metadata.

tools.name: getSuiteSummaryTests
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-summaries/:suiteId/tests — Retrieves summary statistics for all test steps within a specific suite.

**Response Headers:**
- `X-Testable-Count`: Total test count

query_parentSuiteTestId.description: Parent test step ID for hierarchical tests

tools.name: getSuiteTestSummaryErrors
tools.description: [read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-summaries/:suiteId/tests/:suiteTestId/errors — Retrieves all error occurrences for a specific test step within a suite.

tools.name: getSuiteTestSummaryAnnotations
tools.description: [read] GET /executions/:executionId/suite-summaries/:suiteId/tests/:suiteTestId/annotations — Retrieves all annotations (metadata, tags, custom markers) for a specific test step.

tools.name: getExecutionFailedSuiteResults
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/failed-suite-results — Retrieves all failed suite results from the execution.
Same filtering and format options as regular suite results endpoint.

tools.name: getExecutionFailedThreads
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/failed-threads — Retrieves list of virtual user threads that had at least one failed test assertion.

**Use Cases:** Identify which users encountered failures; Debug user-specific test issues; Analyze failure distribution

tools.name: getExecutionFailedUsers
tools.description: [read] GET /executions/:executionId/failed-users — Retrieves list of global user numbers that had at least one failed test assertion.

tools.name: getThreadFailedIterations
tools.description: [read] GET /executions/:executionId/threads/:threadId/failed-iterations — Retrieves all iterations with failed test assertions for a specific virtual user thread.

tools.name: getCommandStream
tools.description:
[read] GET /command-streams/:streamId — Retrieves detailed information about a command stream (browser automation session).
Command streams represent browser automation sessions with multiple commands executed.

**Use Cases:** View complete browser session; Analyze automation command sequence; Debug browser test flows

tools.name: getCommand
tools.description:
[read] GET /commands/:commandId — Retrieves detailed information about a single browser automation command.

**Command Types:**
- Navigation (goto, goBack, goForward)
- Interaction (click, type, select)
- Wait conditions
- Script execution
- Screenshots
- Custom commands

tools.name: getCommandStreamCommands
tools.description:
[read] GET /command-streams/:streamId/commands — Retrieves all commands executed within a command stream.

**Response Headers:**
- `X-Testable-Count-Success`: Successful command count
- `X-Testable-Count-Failure`: Failed command count
- `X-Testable-DetailedCount`: Total detailed count (if not detailed)

**CSV Export:**
Add .csv extension for CSV format.

tools.name: getExecutionCommandStreams
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/command-streams — Retrieves all command streams (browser automation sessions) from the execution.
Available in both JSON and CSV formats.

**Filtering:**
- `region`: Filter by execution region
- `browser`: Filter by browser name
- `since`/`until`: Time range filter
- `asc=true`: Sort ascending
- `includeCommands=false`: Include commands in each stream (CSV default: true)
- `detailed=false`: Include detailed info
- `failuresOnly=false`: Only failed streams
- `includeData=false`: Include request/response data
- `offset`/`limit`: Pagination

**Use Cases:** List all browser sessions; Find failed browser automation; Export for analysis

tools.name: getExecutionCommandStreamSummaries
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/command-stream-summaries — Retrieves aggregated summary statistics for browser automation commands grouped by
browser and command type.

**Summary Metrics:**
- Commands passed/failed
- Average duration
- Screenshot count

**CSV Export:**
Add .csv extension with optional `includeErrors` parameter.

tools.name: getExecutionCommandStreamErrors
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/command-stream-errors — Retrieves aggregated error summary for browser automation commands.

**CSV Export:**
Add .csv extension for CSV format.

tools.name: getExecutionFailedCommandStreams
tools.description:
[read] GET /executions/:executionId/failed-command-streams — Retrieves all command streams that had at least one failed command.
Same filtering and format options as regular command streams endpoint.

tools.name: listIntegrations
tools.description:
[read] GET /integrations — Returns all third-party integrations configured for the authenticated organization.

**Integration Types:**
- `Slack` — Post notifications to a Slack channel
- `Teams` — Post notifications to a Microsoft Teams channel
- `SNS` — Publish notifications to an AWS SNS topic
- `NewRelic` — Forward metrics to New Relic
- `Datadog` — Forward metrics to Datadog
- `Dynatrace` — Forward metrics to Dynatrace
- `CloudWatch` — Forward metrics to AWS CloudWatch
- `AwsCodePipeline` — Trigger AWS CodePipeline stages
- `Custom` — Custom integration with arbitrary settings

query_key.description: API key for authentication (alternative to session-based auth).

tools.name: getIntegration
tools.description: [read] GET /integrations/:id — Retrieves the details of a specific integration by ID.

path_id.description: The unique ID of the integration.

query_key.description: API key for authentication (alternative to session-based auth).

tools.name: listVcsRoots
tools.description:
[read] GET /vcs-roots — Returns all version control system (VCS) roots configured for the authenticated
organization. VCS roots define Git repositories that can be linked to test scenarios
for parameterized test execution driven by commits and branches.

Use `includeTracking=true` to also return VCS roots that are used for tracking
(i.e. linked to a running execution for CI/CD integration).

query_key.description: API key for authentication (alternative to session-based auth).

query_includeTracking.description: When `true`, include VCS roots that are linked to an active execution for tracking purposes.

tools.name: getVcsRoot
tools.description: [read] GET /vcs-roots/:id — Retrieves the full details of a specific VCS root by ID.

path_id.description: The unique ID of the VCS root.

query_key.description: API key for authentication (alternative to session-based auth).

tools.name: getVcsRefs
tools.description:
[read] GET /vcs-roots/:id/refs — Retrieves the list of remote Git refs (branches and tags) available for an
existing VCS root using its stored connection settings.

path_id.description: The unique ID of the VCS root.

query_key.description: API key for authentication (alternative to session-based auth).

tools.name: describe_tools
tools.description: [read] POST /mcp/describe_tools — Returns the full MCP tool descriptor (description and inputSchema with parameter types, descriptions, enums) for each requested tool name. Use this to obtain exact argument names and schemas before calling a tool. ALWAYS call describe_tools for a tool before invoking it for the first time. Pass a list of tool names (e.g. from tools/list); unknown names are omitted from the result and listed in unknownTools. Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

toolNames.description: Tool names to describe (e.g. from tools/list). Returns full descriptor for each known tool.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: [read] POST /mcp/search_tools — Searches the available tool catalog by keyword and returns matching tool names with short descriptions. Use this to find which tools are relevant to your task before calling describe_tools for full parameter schemas. Pass keywords related to what you want to do (e.g., ["execution", "logs"] to find execution log tools, ["screenshot", "output"] to find screenshot tools). Results are ranked by number of keyword matches. Call describe_tools on the results you want to use. Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

keywords.description: One or more keywords to match against tool names and short descriptions. A tool is included if it matches at least one keyword.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching tools to return, sorted by relevance. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: encode_base64
tools.description: [read] POST /encode-base64 — Encodes one or more text strings to base64. Provide either 'text' (single string) or 'texts' (array of strings) to encode multiple at once. Use for file contents or any text data. Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

text.description: The text string to encode to base64. Omit if using 'texts'.

texts.description: Array of text strings to encode. Omit if using 'text'. Returns results array.

tools.name: decode_base64
tools.description: [read] POST /decode-base64 — Decodes one or more base64 strings to text. Provide either 'encoded' (single string) or 'encodedStrings' (array) to decode multiple at once. Use to read or verify base64 content. Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

encoded.description: The base64-encoded string to decode. Omit if using 'encodedStrings'.

encodedStrings.description: Array of base64 strings to decode. Omit if using 'encoded'. Returns results array; failed items have an 'error' field.

tools.name: resolve_openfin_version
tools.description:
[read] POST /resolve-openfin-version — Resolves an OpenFin runtime version to the matching chromedriver version (for Selenium) and Puppeteer version.

The version you pass can be full (e.g. 31.1.1.21) or major only (e.g. 31). The tool extracts the major
version before lookup, so 31.1.1.21 and 31 both resolve to the same driver and Puppeteer versions.

Use this when configuring browser automation for OpenFin desktop apps: you need the driver version for
Selenium or the Puppeteer version for Puppeteer to match the OpenFin/Chromium version. Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

version.description: OpenFin version (e.g. 31, 31.1.1.21). Major version is used for lookup.

tools.name: browser_pages
tools.description:
[read] POST /internal/browser — List all pages (windows/tabs) currently open in the browser session.

Returns each page's index, title, and URL. This is essential for OpenFin testing,
where launching the app opens multiple windows simultaneously (e.g. a main window
and one or more child windows). Use this tool to discover which windows are available,
then call browser_switch_page to select the one you want to interact with.

Example OpenFin workflow:
1. browser_launch(openfinConfigUrl="...") -> sessionId
2. browser_pages(sessionId) -> [{index:0, title:"Hello OpenFin", url:"..."}, ...]
3. browser_switch_page(sessionId, title="Hello OpenFin")
4. browser_screenshot / browser_evaluate / browser_click ... Body fields are top-level arguments; do not wrap them in content or body unless the schema explicitly includes that property.

sessionId.description: Session ID returned by browser_launch. Do NOT invent this value — use the one returned by the launch tool.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description:
[read] POST /internal/browser — Take a full-page screenshot and return it as a base64-encoded PNG.

IMPORTANT: The screenshot is automatically displayed to the user in the UI. Do NOT
embed, describe, or repeat the image data in your reply message. Simply acknowledge
